intended_object: An elementary row commutation of (toroidal) grid diagrams, as in Ozsváth–Stipsicz–Szabó, Grid Homology, Ch. 3: G' is obtained from G by swapping two cyclically adjacent rows whose O–X marking segments are non-interleaving. Inferred from the docstring, the module docs and the parallel column version.
explanation: The definition asks for a row a and its cyclic successor finRotate n a, so the wrap-around pair (n−1, 0) is included, as in the toroidal move. The condition a ≠ finRotate n a only excludes the trivial self-swap for n ≤ 1, and no grid diagram of size 1 exists. The pair must satisfy RowsNoninterleaving. That condition reads, in each row, the columns of its O and X markings (via transpose) and applies Grid.Noninterleaving: each endpoint pair lies on one side of the other pair around the circle. The target is G.swapRows, i.e. relabeling rows by the transposition. When the four endpoint columns are distinct, the condition is exactly "the two pairs of points on the circle do not separate each other", the standard condition for a commutation on the torus, and it does not depend on orientation. Caveat: when the two rows' segments share an endpoint column, the test depends on orientation. With p the shared column, q the other end of the row whose O is at p and s the other end of the row whose X is at p, the cyclic order p, q, s is accepted and p, s, q is rejected. I could not confirm how the book's definition treats this case, and these swaps can be obtained from other grid moves, so it is not a confident discrepancy. Row and column versions are consistent under transpose. The notion is specific to grid diagrams indexed by Fin n, and Mathlib has no counterpart, so it is not too narrow.
